title: Traffic-driven speculative prefetch controller for per-tenant micro-warmups
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a speculative prefetch controller that drives per-tenant micro-warmups using short-term traffic signals and lightweight tenant fingerprints. The controller should decide when to fetch partial model residency (selective layer weights + KV shard ranges) for tenants entering a spike, while avoiding full weight eager-loads across the fleet. Goals: reduce cold-start tail latency on Dedicated instances, preserve throughput guarantees for reserved capacity, and keep memory and network overhead bounded compared to full preheating approaches. The controller will integrate with the fleet admission and autoscaler to respect burst budgets and slot allocation policies.
acceptance_criteria: Controller deployed behind feature flag and enabled for canary tenants
99th percentile cold-start latency for canary tenants reduced by >= 50% compared to baseline without speculative prefetch
Aggregate memory/network overhead of speculative prefetch across fleet <= 20% of baseline full preheat cost for the same traffic pattern
Controller honors tenant burst budgets and never causes slot eviction that violates throughput SLOs
Observability: per-tenant prefetch decisions, fetched segments, and outcomes emitted to Console dashboards with trace links
comments: 2026-02-16 - Kickoff: scoped approach to use short moving-window traffic features (rps slope, recent qps bursts, session reuse) and tenant fingerprint vector computed from recent request signatures.

2026-02-22 - Spike results: offline simulation on 7 days of production traces shows speculative selective-residency reduces average weight bytes fetched per spike by 65% while covering 72% of hot-token sequences within first 3s.

2026-02-28 - Design review: PM and Runtime leads prefer a conservative admission policy that falls back to regular autoscaler if prefetch budget exhausted; agreed to add a hard global prefetch cap per-region.

2026-03-03 - Implementation: added prefetch admission queue, per-tenant credit accounting, and an API endpoint /prefetch-request for runtime agents to request speculative residency slots (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7456).

2026-03-07 - Canary rollout started for 15 tenants on us-west-2 dedicated pool behind feature flag 'spec-prefetch-v1'. Initial telemetry: 99p cold-start latency improved ~48% but we observed a 3% increase in network egress during peak hours.
2026-03-09 - Follow-up: adjusted resident selection strategy to prioritize KV-shard contiguous ranges and top-3 attention blocks; network overhead dropped to 1.4% while 99p latency maintained.
2026-03-10 - Blocker noted: KMS-dependant tenants show slightly slower partial restores when models are encrypted-at-rest; filed ENG-75212 as dependency to optimize encrypted snapshot restore paths.
